entries.proposition: Two DLTs were reported in cycle 1: a grade 3 alkaline phosphatase elevation at 21 mg and, at 42 mg, encephalopathy with grade 3 hepatic failure meeting Hy law criteria (one hepatic DLT at 42 mg, not several). The 42 mg level was discontinued for potential serious liver injury although MTD criteria were not met, and 21 mg (15 patients) was declared the MTD/RP2D.
entries.snippet: One patient developed grade 3 alkaline phosphatase elevation at the 21 mg dose following treatment with BTX A51 that resolved to baseline 4 days after holding treatment. Another patient experienced encephalopathy and grade 3 hepatic failure with AST, ALT, and bilirubin elevations meeting criteria for Hy’s law at the 42 mg dose. The patient’s liver studies and encephalopathy resolved within 2 weeks after discontinuing BTX A51. Due to the potential for serious drug-induced liver injury, the 42 mg dose level was discontinued, even though the criteria for the MTD were not met. After a total of 15 patients enrolled on the next highest dose level 21 mg, the phase 1a trial was stopped and 21 mg administered 3 days per week for 28 days out of a 28-day cycle was declared the MTD/ RP2D.

contradicts_locator.what_changed: Proposition said hepatic DLTs (plural) at 42 mg; the source reports one hepatic DLT at 42 mg and a second DLT (alkaline phosphatase) at 21 mg. Quote widened to the contiguous passage that carries both DLTs, the discontinuation and the RP2D sentence.

entries.proposition: Eleven deaths occurred during treatment and within 28 days of the last dose; five were attributed to disease progression and six occurred without overt progression (lung infection, cardiac arrest, intracranial hemorrhage, fungal infection, septic shock). The body sentence gives no attribution to the drug; the Abstract of the same paper states that no treatment-related deaths occurred (an abstract statement, not a body locator).
entries.snippet: Overall, there were 11 deaths among patients during the study treatment and within 28 days of the last dose. Five of these deaths were attributed to disease progression. Six deaths occurred in the absence of overt disease progression due to lung infection, cardiac arrest, intracranial hemorrhage, fungal infection, and septic shock.

entries.proposition: The text states that A51 lowered Pol II CTD phosphorylation at Ser2 or Ser5 in five AML lines (Fig. 4) and that this resulted in a marked decrease in MYC and MDM2 expression (a leukaemia system, not neural). entries.proposition: The authors conclude the 21 mg dose may be sufficient for maximum biological effect because, despite the small number of patients at 42 mg, they saw no difference in MIC-1 by ELISA or in MCL1, p53 or RNA polymerase II phosphorylation by immunostaining between 21 and 42 mg. No statistical test is cited; Supplementary Fig 1 shows 42 mg bars of 262, 130 and 1412 percent against about 140-165 at 21 mg.
entries.snippet: Although limited by the small number of patients receiving the 42 mg dose, we did not observe differences in MIC-1 by ELISA or MCL1, p53, RNA polymerase II phosphorylation by immunostaining between patients receiving the 21 and 42 mg dose. Therefore, the 21 mg dose may be sufficient to achieve maximum biological effects.

entries.proposition: Three patients attained complete remission with incomplete count recovery (10%), all at 11 mg or 21 mg (2 of 15 at the RP2D of 21 mg); no response was seen among the five patients treated at 42 mg.
entries.snippet: In this study, the anti-leukemic activity of BTX A51 was most apparent at higher doses. Although peripheral blast count reductions were observed at all dose levels, the three patients attaining complete remission with incomplete count recovery (10%) received BTXA51 at 11 mg or 21 mg. Among patients at the recommended phase II dose of 21 mg, we observed a CRi in 2 out of the 15 patients treated (13%). We did not observe any responses among the five patients treated at the 42 mg dose.

entries.proposition: Supplemental Table 3 as printed (N = 1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 8, 5 patients at 1, 3, 5, 8, 11, 21, 42 mg): Day 5 AUC 43.0, 600, 702, 937, 1820, 3773, 4773 ng*h/mL, i.e. per mg 43.0, 200, 140, 117, 166, 180, 114; Day 1 AUC 36.1, 125, 233, 573, 828, 2137 and BLANK at 42 mg (per mg 36.1 to 101.8); Day 1 Cmax 120 at 21 mg versus 99 at 42 mg, Day 5 Cmax 130 versus 155. Exposure is therefore not constant per mg: it rises more than proportionally from 1 to 21 mg (log-log slope about 1.38 for Day 5 AUC and 1.36 for Day 1 AUC, recomputed here and by the audit) and from 21 to 42 mg the Day 5 AUC rises 1.27-fold (3773 to 4773) for a 2-fold dose, Day 5 Cmax 1.19-fold, Day 1 Cmax falls (0.83-fold). The CVs are 22 to 79 percent and N is 1 at two dose levels, so the table supports neither "dose-proportional between 1 and 42 mg" (entry 6) nor a sub-proportionality test; the earlier note's correction ("sub-proportional at the top level") rests on one 21-versus-42 comparison with n = 8 and 5 and is withdrawn as a general statement.
